assessment:
The platform docs are not usable as a reference today. docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md says of itself that it is outdated, and it still makes wrong claims: that stocker reads every collector's output, that raw data lands in the vault service, and a vault layout keyed by `table=`. docs/ROADMAP.md is a plan that sits outside docs/planning/. Several of its items have already landed (book series, grain/bundle preference, the DATA_VAULT_DIR guard, the seed rebuilds) or name code that no longer exists (`scattered`, `subject`, adapter floors, `.pNN.tar`). It also has broken links (SCOPING.md, a missing CATALOG anchor, BUGS entries that are gone). The infrastructure docs (docker/README.md, modules/infra/README.md and the rabbitmq and redis READMEs) describe another system: node.Dockerfile, npm, DB_* URLs, modules such as archivist and packer, the `redis` hostname, and RABBITMQ_* ports. REST facts are written three times. VOCABULARY.md holds service internals, one of them false (hauler fetches file by file, not whole partitions), and it does not define 'origin', which means two different things. planning/COLD.md tells readers to build commands that already exist.

Two code and config defects surfaced along the way and should be fixed first. (1) docker/prod.node.Dockerfile starts dist/index.js, but every service builds to dist/src/index.js, so every prod image crash-loops. (2) Every .env.example writes `KEY=   # comment` after an empty value. Docker compose reads the comment text as the value; I reproduced this with compose v5.7.1: `QUEUE_USER=  # (required)` gives `'# (required)'`. Copying an example unedited therefore breaks services, for example prospector rejecting PROSPECTOR_VENUES as an unknown venue.

Recommended restructure for the fresh start. (a) Tech docs, present tense only, one home each:
- README.md: what the project is, today's chain in one paragraph (archives -> catalog -> hauler -> stocker -> Parquet vault; WebSocket capture parked; REST and replay not built), how to run it (`tb` for modules via dx/, `./tools` for host tooling via dev/tooling), and a complete docs index.
- DATA_PIPELINE.md: about one page, holding the source-priority principle and the running chain, with no history or plans.
- VOCABULARY.md: definitions only, plus the missing terms.
- Infrastructure docs: rewritten from the compose and Dockerfile sources, with providers described on their own terms and the pack-to-hostname mapping only in modules/infra/README.md.
- REST: per-venue facts only in docs/venues/<VENUE>.md; docs/REST.md stays as a shallow cross-venue summary.
- docs/bitmex/: stays where it is, as a doc of a dataset this repo collected (it names services, so it cannot go under docs/venues/), with its working logs moved out or summarised.
(b) Planning: move ROADMAP.md into docs/planning/, cut every landed item and every broken link, give each open item one home, cut planning/REST.md down to the collector plan, clean BUGS.md and planning/COLD.md, and move mental-model.html out of live planning.
(c) Owner decisions before investing further: whether the queue and cache infra packs are needed at all (no current module uses them; only the parked hoarder, router and pipe would), whether to retire the vault service, and whether to delete the archived bot plans.

Cross-unit notes from the reviewer, out of this unit's scope:
- docs/venues/BYBIT.md:154-155 names 'the prospector', which breaks the venue rule.
- The bybit adapter comment ('No limit was found on this bucket') contradicts BYBIT.md ('It bans an address that asks too fast').
- The prospector compose file has a dangling comment about an HTTP/1.1 ceiling.
- planning/STOCKER.md:110 calls `symbol=` a vault key, but the layout uses a plain `<symbol>/` directory.
- services/.deprecated/README.md is accurate; only its pointer to planning/REST.md should follow DPLT-12.

Sequencing for the implementer: do DPLT-15 (the ROADMAP move) together with DPLT-04, DPLT-17 and DPLT-21, because they all edit ROADMAP.md. DPLT-03 and DPLT-05 share README.md:18-20. DPLT-05, DPLT-12, DPLT-15 and DPLT-20 all touch the README Documentation table.

items.title: Prod Node Dockerfile starts dist/index.js, but every service builds to dist/src/index.js
items.problem: Every service tsconfig is composite with include src/**/* and no rootDir, so tsc writes dist/src/index.js. The prod image sets WORKDIR /app/services/${SERVICE_NAME} and runs `exec node ... dist/index.js`, which fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Compose selects docker/${APP_ENV:-prod}.node.Dockerfile, so any prod deployment, or one with APP_ENV unset, crash-loops under restart: unless-stopped. docker/README.md and each package.json `main` repeat the wrong path.
items.evidence: All nine services (catalog, catalog-ui, hauler, hoarder, pipe, prospector, router, stocker, vault) have dist/src/index.js and no dist/index.js. .dockerignore excludes dist/, and the builder runs `pnpm run build` (tsc -b), so the image has the same layout. The dev entrypoint and each service's `start` script already use dist/src/index.js. Both verifiers confirmed at high.
items.fix: Change the last line of docker/prod.node.Dockerfile to `CMD ["/bin/sh", "-c", "exec node --max-old-space-size=${NODE_MEMORY_MB} dist/src/index.js"]`. In every services/*/package.json, set `main` to `dist/src/index.js` or remove it. In docker/README.md, make the requirement 'entry point compiled to dist/src/index.js'. Do not switch to rootDir: src, which is a larger change and breaks the dev entrypoint and the start scripts.
items.tests: Run `APP_ENV=prod docker compose -f services/stocker/docker/compose.yml build`, then `docker run --rm ls dist/src/index.js`, and check that a prod container stays up. Add a cheap guard (a CI step or test) that asserts services//dist/src/index.js exists after `pnpm build` and that the path in the prod CMD matches it.

items.title: Every .env.example puts comments after empty values, and docker compose reads the comment text as the value
items.problem: Lines of the form `KEY=<spaces># text` do not give an empty value under docker compose's --env-file parser (the mechanism dx uses); the value is the literal string `# text`. Copying an example unedited breaks things. QUEUE_USER, QUEUE_PASS and CACHE_PASS become '# (required)'. DATA_DIR becomes '# Host data root', so the derived bind mounts are invalid and compose aborts with a cryptic 'undefined volume'. PROSPECTOR_VENUES, HAULER_VENUES and STOCKER_VENUES carry comment text, and prospector throws 'unknown venue' (services/prospector/src/config.ts:66). HAULER_LENS, STOCKER_LENS and CATALOG_TOKEN get bogus values.
items.evidence: The first verifier found this while checking DPLT-09 (F10). The consolidator reproduced it with Docker Compose v5.7.1: an env file containing `QUEUE_USER=        # (required)` makes `docker compose config` show `A: '# (required)'`, while a bare `DATA_DIR=` gives `""`. `grep -nE '^[A-Z_]+=\s+#'` finds the 11 lines listed.
items.fix: In the root, archives and warehouse .env.example files, move every comment that follows an empty value onto its own line above the variable, and leave the value truly empty (`KEY=`). Fix any comment content in the same pass (see DPLT-09 and DPLT-10). Check dev/tooling/.env.example for the same pattern; the grep found none there.
items.tests: For each module, run `docker compose -f <compose> --env-file .env.example config` and confirm the empty variables come out as "". Add a lint step in CI or a tooling check that fails on `^[A-Z_]+=\s+#` in any .env.example.

items.title: DATA_PIPELINE.md says it is outdated, still makes wrong claims, and is full of history and plans
items.problem: The doc opens with an 'Outdated, do not use as a reference' banner, which breaks 'only what is true today', yet README.md:25 and :51 still send readers to it. Line 97 says stocker reads every collector's output; line 118 of the same doc and the code say it reads only the archives. 'Where raw lands' presents the vault service as a destination, but no module deploys it. The vault layout says `table=`, while the real key is `dataset=`, with interval, kind, depth and aggregated levels and `<symbol|@>/<YYYYMM>.parquet`. Lines 82, 116-125, 139-142 and 144-159 are history or plans.
items.evidence: services/stocker/src/config.ts sets only archivesDir, vaultDir and catalogApi. services/stocker/src/vault.ts:13-14 has the real layout. modules/collect/archives/compose.yml and modules/store/warehouse/compose.yml do not include services/vault. VAULT_URL appears only in .deprecated/scribe and tardy.
items.fix:
Rewrite docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md in the present tense, about one page, and remove the banner.
1. Keep the two-layer intro (13-28) and Source priority (30-47) as the single home of the bulk -> REST -> WS principle. Reduce README.md:12-16 and planning/REST.md:20-31 to a pointer each.
2. Keep the Collectors table. Replace 63-65 with 'hoarder is not deployed by any module'.
3. Replace 'Where raw lands' (80-93) with two entries. The archives: host directories hauler writes, pointing to HAULER.md. The Parquet vault: stocker's. Mention the vault service only as the layout BitMEX's collected data is in, pointing to bitmex/README.md and services/VAULT.md.
4. Line 97: '[stocker] reads the archives and writes one partitioned Parquet vault'. Partitioning bullet: 'Hive keys venue=, market=, dataset=, then interval=, kind=, depth= or aggregated= where the table has one; one directory per instrument (`@` for venue-wide files), one file per month', pointing to STOCKER.md or STOCKER-PARTITIONS.md.
5. Delete 116-125, 139-142 and 144-159. Reduce Replay to 'Replay is not built', with a pointer to the roadmap. Move any wanted plans to docs/planning/.
6. Fix README.md:18-20 to 'One service, stocker, reads the archives ...'.
items.tests: Grep the rewritten doc for 'was', 'once', 'will', 'yet', 'table=', 'origin' and 'Outdated'. Rerun the link check over docs/.

items.title: docker/README.md describes a Dockerfile and an npm build that do not exist
items.problem: The README documents node.Dockerfile, npm ci, a prod-only install and a 'minimal final image'. The real files are dev/prod.node and dev/prod.python Dockerfiles chosen by APP_ENV. The prod build uses pnpm and copies the whole built workspace. The dev image (runs from the /live bind mount through docker/node/entrypoint.sh, with dist built on the host first) is undocumented. The .dockerignore list is wrong.
items.evidence: `ls docker` lists dev.node.Dockerfile, prod.node.Dockerfile, dev.python.Dockerfile, prod.python.Dockerfile, node/entrypoint.sh and python/entrypoint.sh. prod.node.Dockerfile does `RUN pnpm install`, then `COPY --from=builder /app .`. .dockerignore lists .env, .env.local, .env.*.local, docs/ and README.md.
items.fix:
Rewrite the README around what exists:
1. Compose selects `docker/${APP_ENV:-prod}.node.Dockerfile`, and the root .env.example sets APP_ENV=dev.
2. dev: runtime only (node 22-alpine with dumb-init, curl, bash and corepack), runs as `node` from /live through entrypoint.sh, and starts services/$SERVICE_NAME/dist/src/index.js. Build on the host first with `pnpm build`.
3. prod: a builder stage (pnpm install, pnpm run build), then a runtime stage with the whole workspace, starting dist/src/index.js (see DPLT-01).
4. Build args: SERVICE_NAME (required) and NODE_MEMORY_MB (default 2048). Port 3000 is exposed for health.
5. List the real .dockerignore entries.
6. Mention the Python variants (uv sync) in one line.
7. Change the compose snippet to `dockerfile: docker/${APP_ENV:-prod}.node.Dockerfile`.
8. Delete the npm and minimal-image claims.
items.tests: Grep the README for 'npm' and 'node.Dockerfile' with no prefix. Check each listed file exists.

items.title: modules/infra/README.md describes packs, hostnames, variables and modules that do not exist
items.problem: The README says the local pack provides `queue`, but that service is commented out. It gives the cache hostname as `redis`, but local names it `cache`. It documents DB_* URLs, and there is no database. It names modules that do not exist (archivist, collector, archeologist, packer, gui, concierge, student, witness). Its in-page anchors are broken. Its replay and REST statements are plans written as fact. 'Start the infra pack before the app modules' is true of no current module, since archives and warehouse need no pack.
items.evidence: In modules/infra/local/compose.yml the queue service is commented out, and cache is `container_name: cache`. The market pack includes services/redis/docker/compose.yml (service `redis`). No DB_* variable exists anywhere. The only modules are collect/archives and store/warehouse.
items.fix:
Rewrite the README to cover only what the compose files provide, as one table of pack -> services (hostnames):
- local: queue-rt, cache
- store: queue, queue-rt
- market: queue, queue-rt, redis
- bootcamp: queue-rt
- shuttle: queue
Then state that the current modules (archives, warehouse) need no infra pack, and that the broker is used only by hoarder, router and pipe (QUEUE_URL -> host `queue`). This README is the consumer-side home of that mapping. Delete the DB_* paragraphs, the nonexistent module names, the replay and REST claims, and the per-pack sections and their anchors. Also fix the stale header comments in local/compose.yml and shuttle/compose.yml. Compose changes are owner decisions (DPLT-23).
items.tests:
Run a link check. Check every hostname in the table with `docker compose -f modules/infra/

/compose.yml config --services`.

items.title: Root .env.example: dead variables, wrong role notes, and DATA_DIR not guarded
items.problem: REGISTRY_* variables are read by nothing. QUEUE_RT_URL is read by nothing. The VAULT_* variables serve only services/vault, which no module deploys. The role notes are wrong: local has no `queue`, and no pack runs a registry. DATA_DIR is not marked required, and the `:?` guards sit on the derived DATA_ARCHIVES_DIR and DATA_VAULT_DIR. Once DPLT-02 is fixed, a truly empty DATA_DIR yields /archives and /vault, which pass those guards and get bind-mounted at the host root.
items.evidence: `grep -rln REGISTRY_` matches only .env.example. QUEUE_RT_URL appears only in .env.example and in modules/infra/README.md:33. The verifier tested this: with a bare `DATA_DIR=`, compose mounts /archives. The containers run as uid 1000 against that root-owned directory, so they get EACCES rather than writing to the root filesystem.
items.fix:
- Mark DATA_DIR as required in a comment on its own line above the variable.
- Guard DATA_DIR itself in the hauler and stocker compose files (`${DATA_DIR:?DATA_DIR is not defined}`), or require DATA_ARCHIVES_DIR and DATA_VAULT_DIR explicitly instead of deriving them.
- Delete the REGISTRY section and QUEUE_RT_URL.
- Mark the Vault Service section as the settings of services/vault, which no module deploys. Deleting it depends on DPLT-25.
- Correct the role notes: queue -> store, market, shuttle; queue-rt -> local, store, market, bootcamp; cache -> local (as `cache`) and market (as `redis`).
items.tests: With `DATA_DIR=` empty, `docker compose ... config` for hauler and stocker must fail with 'DATA_DIR is not defined'. `grep -rn REGISTRY_` should return nothing.

items.title: archives .env.example: CATALOG_DIR default that does not exist, and a venue list missing bitget
items.problem: The comment says CATALOG_DIR 'defaults under the shared data root'. Nothing supplies that default, and both the prospector and catalog compose files use `${CATALOG_DIR:?...}`, so compose aborts. The PROSPECTOR_VENUES list omits bitget, which prospector registers.
items.evidence: The root .env.example has no CATALOG_DIR. services/prospector/docker/compose.yml:61 and services/catalog/docker/compose.yml:39 both guard it with `:?`. services/prospector/src/venues.ts:32 registers bitget.
items.fix:
- Replace lines 9-11 with: 'Required: compose refuses to start without it. Any absolute path works; the container path is fixed and private.' Do not mention the cold tooling here; its fallback belongs in dev/tooling/.env.example.
- Alternatively, add `CATALOG_DIR=${DATA_DIR}/catalog` to the root .env.example, and only then say it has a default.
- Line 42: move the comment above the variable (DPLT-02) and list binance,bitget,bybit,gate,htx,kucoin,okx. Do the same for 48-49.
items.tests: `docker compose --env-file` config with CATALOG_DIR empty should give the documented error. Diff the venue list against VENUE_NAMES in services/prospector/src/venues.ts.

items.title: The host cold tooling falls back to catalog port 9010, but the archives example leaves CATALOG_PORT empty, which means a random port
items.problem: tools cold runs on the host. It reads CATALOG_PORT from modules/collect/archives/.env and falls back to 9010. With the empty value the example recommends, docker publishes the catalog on a random port, and every catalog call from cold push, evict, pull and audit fails to connect. The consumer's doc (dev/tooling/.env.example) never says it needs a fixed port.
items.evidence: config.ts: `getEnv('CATALOG_URL','') || `http://localhost:${archives['CATALOG_PORT'] || 9010}``. The catalog compose publishes `${CATALOG_PORT:-}:8080`.
items.fix:
- Fix the consumer side first. In dev/tooling/.env.example above CATALOG_URL, write: 'The tooling runs on the host, outside the docker network, so it needs the catalog on a known host port. Unset, CATALOG_URL is http://localhost:<CATALOG_PORT from modules/collect/archives/.env>, or 9010 when that is empty. Set CATALOG_PORT in the archives module on any host where tools cold runs, or set CATALOG_URL here.' Mirror this in docs/tooling/COLD.md if it covers configuration.
- In the archives .env.example, drop 'which is the right answer', or set `CATALOG_PORT=9010` as the example value, without naming tools cold.
- Optional: make the tooling fail with a clear message instead of guessing 9010.
items.tests: With CATALOG_PORT empty, a cold command should produce a clear message, if the optional guard is added. With CATALOG_PORT=9010, `tools cold audit` reaches the catalog.

items.title: VOCABULARY.md describes how services and tools work, and the Partition and Revision entries are false
items.problem: Partition says it is 'downloaded ... whole, or not at all', but hauler fetches file by file and a partition can be half on disk. Revision says it changes with 'how it is stocked', but versions.ts says the opposite. The Run, Snapshot and Catalog entries describe service internals, which CLAUDE.md forbids in VOCABULARY.md.
items.evidence: services/hauler/src has no notion of a partition. fetch.ts writes .part and .bak per file. services/stocker/src/versions.ts:6-22 says a revision never moves for a change to the code that produces it. services/catalog/src/api/listings.ts serves 'the catalog as one S3 bucket', so the Catalog line is accurate, though internal. The hauler comments that say 'each venue as a bucket' are the inconsistent ones.
items.fix:
- Partition: keep the definition. Replace the 'atom' sentence with 'the unit the catalog versions and the vault is stocked in', or drop it.
- Revision: 'What identifies one stocking of a partition in the vault. It changes when the partition's version does, or when what stocking writes for it changes.'
- Run: 'One pass of discovery over a venue's archives.' Move the one-unfinished-run rule to docs/services/PROSPECTOR.md.
- Snapshot: 'The catalog's database as it was at one moment, whole.' Move the incremental mechanics to docs/tooling/COLD-CATALOG.md.
- Catalog: 'The record of every file each venue's archives publish, each under its canonical key.' Move the one-bucket API to docs/services/CATALOG.md.
- Check the hauler 'bucket per venue' comments against the one-bucket listing.
items.tests: Grep docs/ for anything that relies on the old Partition or Revision wording.

items.title: services/rabbitmq/README.md gets the version, port variables, hostname and env file wrong
items.problem: The README says version 3.13; the image is 3.12. It documents RABBITMQ_AMQP_PORT and RABBITMQ_MGMT_PORT with fixed defaults; the compose files use QUEUE_PORT and QUEUE_MGMT_PORT, empty by default, so docker assigns the port. Its hoarder example is invented, it places the credentials in the module .env when they are in the root .env, and it tells readers to edit QUEUE_URL in every service when that value is derived once. It also lists consumers, which a provider doc must not do.
items.evidence: base.yml: `rabbitmq:3.12-management-alpine`. compose.yml: `"${QUEUE_PORT:-}:5672"`. The RABBITMQ_* variables exist only in the test harness (shared/utils/src/testing/docker/rabbitmq.yml, plus the pipe and router .env.testing files).
items.fix:
Rewrite the README on the service's own terms:

items.title: services/redis/README.md has wrong commands, defaults and hostname
items.problem: The README says to build the image, but the compose file uses redis:7-alpine and has nothing to build. It gives CACHE_PORT a default of 6379; empty means docker assigns a port. `tb up infra` is not a module. The connection-string section uses host `redis`, while CACHE_URL uses `cache`. No live service uses Redis.
items.evidence: services/redis/docker/compose.yml: `image: redis:7-alpine`, `"${CACHE_PORT:-}:6379"`. dx/utils/discovery.js registers only directories that contain a compose.yml, and modules/infra has none. services/stocker/src/service.ts:6 sets `redis: false`.
items.fix:
Cut the README to the service on its own terms:
- Redis 7 alpine with AOF.
- The password comes from CACHE_PASS; empty leaves auth off.
- Port 6379 is published on CACHE_PORT; empty means docker assigns one.
- Data lives in the `redis-data` volume.
- The service name and hostname in compose.yml are `redis`.
Delete the build block, the `tb up infra` example and the connection section. Do not name packs or consumers; that belongs in modules/infra/README.md.
items.tests: `grep -n 'tb up infra\|docker build' services/redis/README.md` should return nothing.

items.title: Infra packs: local's queue is commented out, the cache hostname differs between packs, and no current module uses either
items.problem: The local pack has no `queue`, although QUEUE_URL points at host `queue`. The market pack's redis has no `cache` hostname, so the root CACHE_URL (`@cache:6379`) does not resolve there. Only the parked hoarder, router and pipe would use the broker, and no service config reads CACHE_URL.
items.evidence: See DPLT-08 and DPLT-22. The F7 verifier noted that these compose changes are a configuration decision for the owner.
items.fix: Once the owner decides: either uncomment `queue` in local and add `hostname: cache` (or a network alias) to the market pack's redis, or remove the queue and cache packs that nothing uses and cut the related .env.example sections and READMEs.
items.tests: For each pack, `docker compose config` should show hostnames that match QUEUE_URL and CACHE_URL.
items.owner_question: Are the queue and cache infra packs still wanted? If so, should local run `queue`, and should the cache be reachable as `cache` in every pack? If not, delete the packs and their docs instead of rewriting them.
